criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Strongest work is the measured relief. Slide 6 shows 12 capped discs, 4 discs plus a D half, and 19 gold-rimmed discs running off the right edge. It reads at feed size without labels. Slide 9's empty IN SERVICE recess is a real visual argument. Slides 1, 3 and 5 are finished, true-scale wafer boats in one floodlit pool. The value register is genuinely dark: preflight measured mid 0.059, 0.061 and 0.032 on frames 1, 6 and 9. Two frames fail the showstopper test outright. Slide 8 leans on a primitive lumpy head model cropped at the left edge, beside a stock laptop. Its black wafer boat is black on black and shows nothing of 'servers working as one system'. Slide 7 is a small copper cut-out, about 15 percent of the frame, floating on diagonal grooved stone. It does not read as crystal growth and fills well under a third of the frame. Slide 2's 'Lubbock County' label sits on the footer baseline between 'c3 c18 c19' and the URL, so type is crowded into the folio row. Slides 3 and 4 have plum-black wafers on a near-black bench with no single bright edge. Slide 4's twelve plus twelve split reads by label rather than by light. Slide 1's lowest 30 percent is dead bench, which preflight itself flagged. Machine QA also flagged slide 6's labels as outside the 80 px safe zone, at x=32.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: Clearly one deck. One lab bench, one floodlit warm key and one dark grade carry it, and the measured scale of one wafer per $1 million runs through slides 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6. The open-ended boat motif changes state from cover (rods run past the last wafer) to slide 3 (capped) to slide 5 (cleaved half) to slide 6 (open channel). The value track holds dark with no strobe. Three frames sit outside that vocabulary: slide 2 is a stucco tile relief, slide 7 a copper blob on grooved stone, and slide 8 a desk scene with a figure. In the filmstrip, 7 and 8 read as borrowed from another deck.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces to a claim. Slide 6's $12M, $4.5M and $19M trace to c15, c17 and c1. $24M traces to c16, 2023 to c19, and November 13th to c2. All 19 claims are primary Texas Tech Now pages with verbatim quotes. 'Over', 'roughly' and 'exact' are kept faithfully, and slide 6 declines to draw a total. One phrasing leans slightly past the source. c4's 'not built yet' and the cover headline infer construction status from 'will help establish', which supports but does not state it.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: What, who and where are clear: the Texas CHIPS Office in the Office of the Governor, Texas Tech, and Lubbock (slide 2). The amounts and the missing date are concrete. Nothing tells a reader what they can do next. There is no meeting, no next filing and no body to watch, and the close only asks 'When does Texas Tech put a date on it?'

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe with '$19 million for a cluster not built yet' and slide 2 places it. Slides 3 to 6 build to the turn on slide 6, 'three kinds of number'. The close's empty recess lands. Slide 8 partly restates content the close's 'CHIPS, PER THE DEAN' row carries, so it could move or merge with little loss.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean, sourced and on register, and 'Lubbock has a computing cluster on paper' is a good open. Much of the copy reads as institutional paraphrase: 'administered by the Texas CHIPS Office in the Office of the Governor', and the 'Drawn to illustrate' tag repeated on six frames. There is little South Plains texture beyond the place name.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: This is an interior floodlit lab bench with small true-scale objects and reliefs. Nos. 74 to 76 were lastLight exteriors and no. 73 was server hardware, per art_preflight plan.distinct_from_recent, so it is a fresh technique and opening move. The one familiar move is the nameplate-with-empty-slot close.

one_sentence_fix: Rebuild slides 7 and 8 inside the wafer-bench vocabulary instead of borrowing a copper cut-out and a primitive figure at a laptop: for 7, a single wafer under a lit epitaxy susceptor with a visible grown layer edge filling half the frame, and for 8, the nineteen-wafer boat beside a row of empty, unlit server sled bays on the same bench, so the deck's measured-scale argument carries through to the close.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A primitive lumpy head model cropped at the left edge and a stock laptop are the subject. The black carbide wafer boat merges into the shadow, and nothing shows a cluster of servers working as one system.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Delete the head and the laptop. Stand the floodlit boat in front of a short row of empty sled bays on the same epoxy bench, with a warm rim light on the bay edges so the boat silhouettes against them.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The subject is a small copper cut-out (about 15 percent of the frame) floating on diagonal grooved stone. It does not read as crystal growth, has no scale and no contact shadow, and leaves the lower half a dead texture field.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Replace it with one large wafer, filling a third to a half of the frame and seen at a raking angle on a lit susceptor. Give it a visibly thicker grown epitaxial layer stepping across its face, cast onto the bench by the same warm key as slides 1 to 5.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The 'Lubbock County' label sits on the footer baseline between the cite line and the URL, so three runs of type collide in the folio row. The tile grid alone does not tell a reader it is the Panhandle county grid.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move the label up inside the lit copper tile's top edge. Pull the camera back so the grid's irregular state edge or the neighbouring county outlines enter the frame and read as Texas.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Twenty-four plum-black wafers sit on a near-black bench with no bright edge. The quartz-versus-carbide boat distinction reads only through the 'state' and 'Texas Tech' labels, not through light.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Swing the key to rake across the wafer tops so each rim catches a lit arc, as on slide 5. Put a warm strip behind the clear quartz boat so its glass reads against the opaque carbide one.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The lowest 30 percent of the frame is unlit dead bench under the boat, and the wafer faces are dim plum on black.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the camera and push the boat down into the frame so it fills the lower band. Add the fine epoxy scratches and a floodlit sheen under it that preflight already proposed.
